skill.name: hooks-automation
skill.description: Automates Claude Code hook workflows with Claude Flow commands for pre-operation checks, post-operation formatting, session persistence, Git quality gates, MCP coordination, and memory updates.
skill.summary: Coordinate Claude Code hooks, agent workflows, memory, Git checks, and session automation.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, and ordinary Git hook examples. One production environment file example remains sensitive, and semantic review found unsafe shell interpolation plus possible secret retention in logs and memory. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill text.

remediation.issue: Raw tool parameters are interpolated into shell command strings.
remediation.suggestion: Use argument arrays, strict escaping, and allowlists for paths, commands, task text, and search patterns before hooks execute.

remediation.issue: Examples reference production environment files and command output logging.
remediation.suggestion: Add manual approval, secret redaction, and protected-file deny rules for env files, logs, summaries, metrics, and memory entries.

remediation.issue: Destructive cleanup commands appear in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace destructive examples with harmless commands or document path allowlists and confirmation requirements before cleanup runs.

remediation.issue: Git hook examples rely on external CLI commands.
remediation.suggestion: Pin tool versions, document installation trust requirements, and fail closed when required binaries or MCP services are unavailable.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Interpolation in Hook Commands
semantic_findings.description: Settings examples interpolate tool parameters such as file paths, commands, tasks, and search patterns into shell command strings. A crafted parameter could break quoting and run unintended shell commands when hooks execute.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple examples place untrusted Claude Code tool parameters inside shell command strings. The documentation does not show escaping, argument arrays, or allowlists.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Data Retention in Logs and Memory
semantic_findings.description: The skill describes logging command output, storing command results, and exporting session metrics and summaries. Without redaction, these hooks can persist secrets from command output, file paths, or build logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections explicitly enable command-output logging, result storage, and session export. No redaction controls are documented near those examples.

content.value_statement: Manual hook setup can leave agent work inconsistent and hard to trace. This skill documents Claude Flow hooks for coordination, formatting, memory, and session automation.
actual_capabilities: Shows pre-task, pre-edit, pre-bash, post-edit, post-task, and session hook commands.
Provides Claude settings examples for PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, and SessionEnd hooks.
Demonstrates MCP memory usage, agent spawning, swarm status, and neural training integration.
Includes Git pre-commit, post-commit, and pre-push hook examples for quality checks.
Explains protected file handling, automatic testing hooks, debugging commands, and troubleshooting steps.
limitations: This skill is documentation only and does not include a tested hook implementation package.
Examples assume claude-flow alpha, Claude Code hooks, and optional MCP servers are already configured.
Hook commands may run shell commands, so users must review quoting, escaping, and permissions.
The skill does not prove that memory storage redacts secrets before persistence.

use_cases.title: Standardize AI Coding Workflows
use_cases.description: Use pre-edit and post-edit hooks to validate files, format changes, and record decisions across repeated coding tasks.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Projects
use_cases.description: Use task, session, memory, and notification hooks to keep specialized agents aligned during larger implementation work.

use_cases.title: Add Git Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Use documented Git hook examples to run validation, tests, metrics, and notifications before commits or pushes.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Basic Hooks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a project that does not use hooks yet.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hooks-automation skill to outline a minimal Claude Code hook setup for my project. Include pre-edit, post-edit, and session-end steps.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Memory Coordination
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for agents that share task state.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hooks-automation skill to design a memory coordination plan for three agents working on one feature. Include memory keys and session steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Git Quality Gates
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for commit and push checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hooks-automation skill to propose Git hook quality gates for a JavaScript repository. Include tests, formatting, metrics, and failure behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Hook Security
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert review before enabling shell-based hooks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hooks-automation skill to review my planned hook commands for shell injection, secret exposure, unsafe file access, and overly broad automation.

output_examples.input: Request: Configure pre-edit and post-edit hooks for a JavaScript project.
output_examples.output: A setup plan with validation before edits, formatting after edits, memory keys for changed files, and a short test checklist.

output_examples.input: Request: Coordinate backend, frontend, and test agents during one feature build.
output_examples.output: A workflow that starts a shared session, assigns agents, stores implementation notes, restores context, and broadcasts completion status.

output_examples.input: Request: Harden a hook configuration before enabling it.
output_examples.output: A risk review that flags unsafe interpolation, sensitive file access, command logging, and missing confirmation for destructive operations.

best_practices: Pin and review the claude-flow version before enabling automated hooks.
Escape or avoid shell interpolation for file paths, task text, search patterns, and commands.
Redact secrets from command output, memory entries, metrics, and generated summaries.
anti_patterns: Do not pass raw tool parameters directly into shell command strings.
Do not run hooks against production environment files without manual approval and redaction.
Do not enable destructive cleanup commands without path allowlists and confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It documents Claude Flow hook workflows for validation, formatting, memory coordination, session management, Git checks, and agent coordination.

faq.question: Does it install Claude Flow for me?
faq.answer: No. It assumes the Claude Flow CLI and any needed MCP servers are installed and available.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes, Codex can use the documentation to plan, review, or adapt hook workflows for compatible projects.

faq.question: Are the hook examples safe to copy directly?
faq.answer: Review them first. Several examples use shell commands and raw parameter interpolation that should be hardened before use.

faq.question: What projects benefit most from this skill?
faq.answer: It is most useful for repositories that rely on Claude Code, agent workflows, Git quality gates, and persistent coordination memory.

faq.question: What should I check before enabling hooks?
faq.answer: Check command quoting, package versions, file permissions, secret redaction, timeout behavior, and manual approval for risky actions.
